there are generally strong negative societal attitudes towards pregnancy among women with disabilities, which is influenced by their perceived cause of disability.
the majority of respondents agreed that PWDs should be kept in a special institution until delivery to avoid the transmission of disability.
community perceptions towards pregnant women living in Ghana with disabilities are generally negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social construction of disability, the social exclusion of PWDs and the need for social change.
the social exclusion of PWDs, especially with regard of the sexual and reproductive health of PWDs and their right to a safe motherhood.
the need for a more inclusive approach in the provision of health services to pregnant women living with disability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the community attitudes towards the pregnancy of PWD is negative, and that this may have an impact on the reproductive rights of women with disabilities.

the community has a generally negative attitude to the pregnancy of women with disabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are negative attitudes towards pregnancy in disability and these attitudes are influenced by educational status and perceptions of the causes of disability.
there are negative societal attitudes towards pregnancy of women living disabilities in rural Ghana.
there is a need to create awareness and education about the sexual and reproductive rights of women living with a disability in Ghana.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public perception towards the pregnancy of PWD is generally negative and that this perception is associated with the perceived cause of the disability.
there is an urgent need for a comprehensive public education and awareness campaign to dispel myths and misconceptions about the sexuality and reproductive health of PWDs.
the community needs to be sensitized on the issue of disability, and that women with disabilities should also be supported to be empowered and have access to reproductive health services.
